title: Unfamiliar church caller with donation context

input.content: Someone named Jenny called me claiming to be from the church I go to, but I don't know anyone named Jenny, and the church doesn't normally ask for donations.

title: Direct church donation request through Zelle

input.content: Pastor Mike texted from a new number asking me to donate by Zelle right now for an emergency church fund and not mention it yet.
The school newsletter says the fundraiser link is on the official school website and donations are optional at the front office.
My landlord emailed that rent must be wired today to a new bank account because the old one is frozen.

title: Boss asks for vendor bank change

input.content: My boss says the vendor account changed and I should use the replacement wire instructions immediately.
Mom it's me, this is my new number. I am in an emergency and need you to Cash App me money right now.

title: Friend asks for Facebook reset code

input.content: A friend says they accidentally sent their Facebook reset code to my phone and needs me to read back the login code.
Apple security notice says my Apple ID is locked and I need to verify at http://appleid-security-help.com today.
My dentist office texted to remind me that my appointment is Tuesday at 2 pm. No payment or account information is requested.
A Facebook Marketplace buyer says they overpaid by Venmo business and I need to refund the difference to a shipping agent before pickup.

title: Restaurant menu QR with no payment

input.content: The restaurant table has a QR code for the menu only. It is not asking me to pay or sign in.
A note on the parking meter says the old machine is broken. Scan this QR code to pay the parking ticket fee immediately.
USPS says my package is held for a customs fee and I need to pay today at https://bit.ly/package-fee or delivery fails.
A remote job says I should mobile deposit a cashier's check, buy equipment from their approved vendor, and send back anything left over today.
A recovery expert says they can recover my crypto if I send an upfront fee in USDT and share my private key.
My friend asked if I want lunch Saturday at the usual place. No links, payment, passwords, or codes.
Jenny called. Weird?
An email asks me to open the attached invoice zip file today and enable content so the document displays correctly.
A bank fraud agent called and told me to move my money to a safe account to stop hackers after an unauthorized charge.
Someone claiming to be from the sheriff says there is a warrant and I must buy prepaid gift cards today to avoid arrest.
A charity I have heard of sent a message about a gala donation, but I did not sign up for texts and there is no official website listed.
The electric company says my service will be cancelled in two hours unless I pay with a prepaid card over the phone.
I opened the official Netflix app myself to review my subscription. No one sent me a link or asked for codes.
Someone I met online says they love me and wants me to use their secret trading platform with guaranteed daily returns. They cannot video call.

title: Prize claim requires Google Play card

input.content: Amazon support says I won a prize, but I need to buy a Google Play gift card today and send the card code to claim it.

title: PayPal friends and family protection fee

input.content: The buyer says PayPal needs me to send a friends and family fee first to upgrade my marketplace account before they can pick up the item.
Microsoft support called and says hackers are on my laptop. They told me to install AnyDesk, allow remote access, and open my bank for a refund.
The IRS called saying I will be arrested today unless I wire the money through Western Union before the office closes.
FedEx delivery notice says my shipment needs address confirmation through a tinyurl link or it will be returned today.
Someone says they are my grandson and were arrested after an emergency. They need bail paid with Apple gift cards and say not to tell anyone.

title: New job asks for identity details by email

input.content: A new remote job emailed a payroll setup form asking for my Social Security number, date of birth, bank password, and bank routing number before any interview.
Someone says they need to verify my Cash App account and wants me to send the one-time verification code from my phone.

title: Flyer QR sends donation to unknown wallet

input.content: A flyer says to scan this QR code to donate to a relief fund, but it opens a payment wallet I do not recognize.

title: Ticket seller wants payment outside platform

input.content: A ticket seller on Marketplace says to pay by Venmo friends and family outside the platform because buyer protection is broken.
I got an unexpected shared document link saying I need to validate my login before I can see the file.
My insurance refund message says I must confirm my card details at https://refund-verify.example today to receive the money.
A person I met online says they love me and need an emergency wire transfer for bail. They cannot video call and want this kept between us.
A trading platform shows huge returns but says I must send more crypto for a tax fee before I can withdraw my profit.
My regular vendor sent the monthly invoice from their usual email. I was expecting it and it does not ask me to enable macros, click a new link, or change payment details.
An unknown sender says they attached a zip file with their resume and asks me to open the file today.

title: User checks bank through official app

input.content: I opened my bank's official app myself to check a transaction. No message asked me for codes, payments, links, or passwords.
Netflix billing notice says my payment failed and I need to update billing through this link today or the account will be suspended.
My roommate, who I know in person, reminded me that rent is due and asked me to send the normal Zelle payment we use every month.
This is your manager. Buy Apple gift cards urgently for a client, keep this confidential, and send me the codes.
PayPal security text says there is suspicious activity and asks me to reply with the security code to secure my account.
A toll notice says final notice: scan the QR code to pay a small fee within 2 hours or a large penalty will be added.
A Marketplace seller says I need to pay a Zelle deposit before I can see the apartment, and they will send keys after payment.
Someone says they need help getting back into Facebook and asks me to send them the login code that came to my phone.
A message just says urgent, I need your help today, please call me right now.
Is this okay?
My coworker sent a normal calendar invite for our team meeting next Wednesday. It does not ask for payment, passwords, codes, or a new login.
